knowledge: Neurodevelopmental disorder with poor or absent speech, dysmorphic facies, and behavioral abnormalities (NEDSFB, OMIM #621182) is an autosomal dominant condition caused by heterozygous de novo or inherited pathogenic variants in NAV3 (Neuron Navigator 3, located on chromosome 12q21). Reported individuals exhibit a neurodevelopmental syndrome primarily characterized by global developmental delay, severe expressive speech impairment (ranging from severely delayed speech acquisition to completely absent speech), non-specific or distinctive facial dysmorphisms, variable intellectual disability, and behavioral disturbances such as hyperactivity, aggression, or autism spectrum features. Because the entity was characterized relatively recently, the total reported cohort in published literature is small, likely comprising one or two landmark discovery cohorts describing between 10 and 30 individuals.
prior_hypothesis: A clinical presentation of profound speech impairment disproportionate to motor delay, accompanied by midface retraction or dysmorphic craniofacial features (e.g., prominent forehead, hypertelorism, thin upper lip), and behavioral dysregulation (hyperactivity/autistic traits) creates a high index of suspicion, but phenotypic differentiation from other neurodevelopmental syndromes (e.g., Angelman syndrome, FOXP2-related speech-language disorders, or PACS1/Mowat-Wilson-like presentations) from phenotype alone is insufficient for definitive diagnosis without molecular confirmation of NAV3 variants.

candidate_answers.answer: Core clinical phenotypes consistently reported across affected individuals include severe expressive language impairment or absent speech (HP:0001344 / HP:0000750) in >90% of individuals, intellectual disability/global developmental delay (HP:0001249 / HP:0001263) in virtually 100%, behavioral abnormalities (HP:0000708) including hyperactivity (HP:0000752) and autistic features (HP:0000729) in 60-80%, and variable facial dysmorphism (HP:0001999) in >75% of reported cases.
candidate_answers.aspect: Reported phenotypic spectrum and core frequencies

candidate_answers.answer: The most discriminating clinical hallmark is severe, disproportionate expressive speech failure in the presence of mild-to-moderate gross motor delay and behavioral disinhibition, distinguishing it from classic Angelman syndrome (lacking ataxia, characteristic microcephaly, and paroxysmal laughter) and FOXP2-related speech apraxia (which typically lacks the prominent dysmorphic facial features and severe behavioral disruptions).

Features that are consistently absent or atypical in NAV3-related disease include progressive neurodegeneration, structural brain malformations such as lissencephaly or holoprosencephaly, and severe congenital visceral or cardiac malformations; presence of severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy or progressive regression strongly argues against this specific entity.

Most pathogenic NAV3 alterations are de novo heterozygous missense or truncating/loss-of-function variants, with truncating mutations potentially leading to more severe cognitive and behavioral deficits via haploinsufficiency, while missense variants clustering in functional domains (e.g., AAA domain, CH domain) may present variable expressivity; no established sex-specific differences exist.
candidate_answers.aspect: Genotype-phenotype, variant position, and demographic correlations

candidate_answers.answer: Literature discrepancies primarily concern whether craniofacial dysmorphism constitutes a recognizable, recurrent gestalt versus a non-specific collection of minor anomalies, and whether seizures/epilepsy represent a recurrent feature or merely an incidental finding.
